subject: Physics
name: Physics, Units 3 and 4
about: VCE, Fields, motion, relativity, light and matter
syllabus: VCE Physics Study Design (from 2023), Units 3 and 4

units.title: Unit 3: How do fields explain motion and electricity?

points.title: Forces in two dimensions
points.brief: Newton's laws apply when two or more forces act at angles, by adding the forces as vectors.

points.title: Projectile motion in physics
points.brief: Horizontal and vertical motion are independent: steady horizontal velocity and constant downward acceleration. Air resistance shortens the path.

points.title: Uniform circular motion
points.brief: An object moving in a horizontal circle at steady speed accelerates towards the centre, as a car on a curve or a ball on a string does.

points.title: Banked tracks
points.brief: On a banked curve, part of the normal force supplies the centripetal force, so a car can turn without friction.

points.title: Vertical circular motion
points.brief: At the top and bottom of a vertical loop, the normal force and weight combine to give the centripetal force.

points.title: Impulse and momentum
points.brief: Impulse, force times time, equals the change in momentum, and total momentum is conserved in a straight-line collision.

points.title: Work done by a force
points.brief: Work is force times displacement, or the area under a force-distance graph.

points.title: Elastic and inelastic collisions
points.brief: Kinetic energy is kept in an elastic collision and partly lost in an inelastic one, though momentum is conserved in both.

points.title: Springs and energy
points.brief: Energy moves between kinetic, elastic and gravitational forms, found from equations or the area under force-distance graphs.

points.title: Fields and field lines
points.brief: A field is a region where a force acts. Field lines show direction, and their spacing shows strength.

points.title: Gravitational fields
points.brief: Mass creates a gravitational field, g = GM/r², which pulls other masses toward it.

points.title: Newton's law of universal gravitation
points.brief: F = GMm/r², so the force halves to a quarter when the distance doubles.

points.title: Electric fields
points.brief: The field around a point charge weakens with the inverse square of distance. A uniform field between plates accelerates a charge, with F = qE and W = qV.

points.title: Magnetic fields
points.brief: Magnets and currents create magnetic fields, with field lines from north to south.

points.title: Comparing fields
points.brief: Electric and magnetic forces can attract or repel, but gravity only attracts. Fields can be static or changing, uniform or not.

points.title: Satellites and orbits
points.brief: Gravity supplies the centripetal force for a satellite, which sets its speed and period for each orbit radius.

points.title: Charged particles in fields
points.brief: A charge moving across a magnetic field feels a force F = qvB at right angles, so it moves in a circle whose radius depends on its speed.

points.title: Particle accelerators
points.brief: Accelerators such as synchrotrons speed charges up with electric fields and bend them in circles with magnetic fields.

points.title: Force on a current in a field
points.brief: A current-carrying wire in a magnetic field feels a force, F = nIlB, used in motors.

points.title: DC motors
points.brief: A current-carrying coil in a magnetic field turns, with a split ring commutator keeping it turning. More current, field or loops give more torque.

points.title: Magnetic flux
points.brief: Flux is the field strength times the area it passes through at right angles, Φ = BA.

points.title: Faraday's law
points.brief: A changing flux induces an emf, equal to the number of turns times the rate of change of flux.

points.title: Lenz's law
points.brief: The induced current flows to oppose the change in flux that caused it.

points.title: Generators
points.brief: A coil turning in a magnetic field gives AC through slip rings in an alternator, or DC through a split ring commutator.

points.title: Solar cells and inverters
points.brief: Photovoltaic cells produce DC, and an inverter turns it into AC for use in the home.

points.title: Peak and RMS values
points.brief: The RMS voltage of an AC supply is the peak voltage divided by √2, and gives the same power as that DC voltage.

points.title: Transformers
points.brief: Changing current in one coil induces a voltage in another, Vp/Vs = Np/Ns, stepping voltage up or down.

points.title: Transmission losses
points.brief: Power is lost as heat in wires, P = I²R, so electricity is sent at high voltage and low current.

units.title: Unit 4: How have creative ideas and investigation revolutionised thinking in physics?

points.title: Wave properties
points.brief: Light is a transverse electromagnetic wave made by accelerating charges, and all such waves travel at c in a vacuum.

points.title: Standing waves
points.brief: A wave and its reflection add to make a standing wave with fixed nodes and antinodes.

points.title: Diffraction
points.brief: Waves spread out through a gap or around an edge, most when the gap is close to the wavelength.

points.title: Young's double slit experiment
points.brief: Light through two slits makes bright and dark bands from interference, evidence that light is a wave.

points.title: Path difference and interference
points.brief: Bright bands occur where path difference is a whole number of wavelengths, dark bands at half wavelengths.

points.title: The photoelectric effect
points.brief: Light above a threshold frequency ejects electrons from a metal, whatever its intensity, which a wave model cannot explain.

points.title: Photons and energy
points.brief: Light comes in photons with energy E = hf. A photon's energy goes into freeing the electron and its kinetic energy.

points.title: Work function and stopping voltage
points.brief: The work function is the least energy to free an electron. The stopping voltage measures the electrons' maximum kinetic energy.

points.title: Matter waves
points.brief: De Broglie proposed particles have a wavelength, λ = h/p, so electrons can diffract like light.

points.title: Electron diffraction
points.brief: Electrons passing through a crystal make diffraction patterns, confirming their wave nature.

points.title: Momentum of photons and matter
points.brief: Photons and particles with the same wavelength have the same momentum, p = h/λ.

points.title: The idea of quantisation
points.brief: Energy that comes only in set amounts explained both the behaviour of light and the structure of atoms.

points.title: Atomic energy levels and spectra
points.brief: Electrons in atoms have set energy levels. Moving between them emits or absorbs photons of set frequencies, giving line spectra.

points.title: Wave-particle duality
points.brief: Single photons and single electrons build up a double slit pattern, evidence that light and matter both act as waves and particles.

points.title: Limits of classical mechanics
points.brief: Newton's mechanics fails for objects moving close to the speed of light.

points.title: Einstein's postulates
points.brief: The laws of physics are the same in every inertial frame, and the speed of light is the same for all observers.

points.title: The Michelson-Morley experiment
points.brief: It found no change in the speed of light with Earth's motion, a result that supports special relativity.

points.title: Time dilation and length contraction
points.brief: Proper time and proper length are measured in an object's own frame. Observers moving relative to it measure longer times and shorter lengths.

points.title: Relativity in action
points.brief: Muons reaching the ground, the design of particle accelerators and GPS corrections all depend on relativity.

points.title: Mass and energy in relativity
points.brief: An object's total energy is γmc², its rest energy plus kinetic energy. Mass converts to energy in the Sun and in annihilation.

points.title: Variables and controlled experiments in physics
points.brief: Changing one independent variable, measuring the dependent variable and controlling the rest shows cause and effect.

points.title: Linearising data
points.brief: Graphing transformed data to get a straight line shows a relationship, and the gradient has a physical meaning.

points.title: Presenting a scientific poster
points.brief: A poster communicates an investigation briefly, with correct symbols, units and significant figures, and acknowledges sources.
